criteria.demonstration: The explicit ownership graph distinguishes value and control lifetime, implicit and observer weak references, terminal zero, overflow refusal and caller-owned reference preconditions. The manual release-sequence/final-acquire-fence argument is stated separately from runtime synchronization of the payload and from strong-cycle retention. Safe-language Rc/Arc rules do not become ISO C enforcement.

criteria.demonstration: Both actual retained non-atomic and C17 atomic producer APIs are executed. The new adapter allocates two real controls and two actual typed allocator payloads, preserves the report on raw or typed acquisition failure and unwinds prior owners. It detaches outgoing edges and drains releases after callbacks return, respecting the original non-reentry contract. Initialization publication and transferred owners are explicit in the real pthread clients.

criteria.criterion: Trace every strong/weak boundary with an independent counter model, test maximum-count refusal, and reject omission of the implicit weak release. Run the actual four-thread anchor, separate TSan if available, GCC/Clang optimized and ASan/UBSan builds, inspect atomic lowering and report lock-free status. A quiet race detector does not prove the memory-order argument or reclaim safety for fabricated references.

criteria.criterion: Construct a two-node strong cycle and show retained values after external owners disappear; break one edge with a weak reference and account for both control blocks. Delayed assessment races the last strong drop with weak upgrade using a synchronized start and a live weak owner: outcomes are successful ownership before destruction or DEAD, never resurrection.
